Extract helical/stripe or LO phases, low-T first-order boundary, transverse stiffness instability, critical/Lifshitz endpoints and stability claims, with exact equations and numerical parameter coordinates; distinguish Gaussian necessary stability from global branch freeenergy comparison. Does this source itself cover asymmetry δN=.25(or conversion to αtilde=.25) at T/Tc~.05, and does its published boundary demonstrably preempt another single-q weak/strong helical endpoint in THAT domain? The external Zhuang2026 model is clean2D parabolic Rashba strongSOC/weakfield, helicity Nλ, common vF,plane-wave singlet gap; it reports single-q weak/strong-helical CEP T/Tc≈.05 at αtilde=.25; exact h and qcoordinates currently missing. answers.answer: Supported. The paper uses a clean 2D parabolic Rashba model, H_so=α[σ×p]·n, in-plane Zeeman energy H=gμ_Bh/2, and intraband singlet pairing. Its hierarchy is ε_F≫αp_F≫T_c, with H≪αp_F and q≪p_F. The order parameter contains momenta ±Q, with Q perpendicular to h. The pairing cutoff is ω_D, Matsubara ω=2π(n+1/2)T, and T_c0=2ω_D exp(−1/νU+γ)/π. Plotted H and T are normalized by T_c0; momentum is commonly represented by v_FQ/T_c0.

references.section: II. Model of a spin-orbital superconductor

answers.answer: Supported, with a convention caveat. The helicity Fermi momenta and DOS are p_F^λ=√(2mμ+m²α²)+λmα and ν_λ(ε_F)=ν(ε_F)(1+λα/v_F). The leading phase diagram sets ν_+=ν_− and restores the O(α/v_F) DOS correction only later. From the parabolic dispersion, the zero-field branch velocities at their respective Fermi momenta satisfy v_λ=p_F^λ/m−λα=√(2μ/m+α²), hence are equal; this velocity equality is an inference from the dispersion. If δN is defined as (ν_+−ν_−)/(ν_++ν_−), the source gives δN=α/v_F at this order. It defines neither δN nor the external α-tilde convention.

VIII. Phase diagram in the presence of impurities

answers.answer: Supported. The normal-to-superconducting instability maximizes the quadratic kernel over Q. The Lifshitz point is L=(H_L,T_L)=(1.536,0.651)T_c0 and separates Q=0 from Q≠0. The symmetric point is S=(H_S,T_S)=(1.779,0.525)T_c0 with v_FQ_S=2.647T_c0. Below S, β_a<0 favors a single-helicity helical state; above S, β_a>0 favors the parity-even stripe/LO state proportional to cos(Qy). Nonlinear stripe corrections include odd harmonics ±3Q,±5Q,… .

Supported. The low-temperature helical potential is expanded as Ω_hel(Q)=Ω_hel(0)+aQ²+bQ⁴+cQ⁶. The Q=0 local-stability line LO has a critical endpoint at (H,T)=(1.547,0.455)T_c0 where b=0; below it b<0 and the homogeneous-to-inhomogeneous transition is first order. The authors state that the actual thermodynamic BCS-to-inhomogeneous line O′ lies below the absolute local-stability line O, approximately H_O=1.76T_c0, but do not give a complete O′ coordinate set or global branch comparison.

references.section: V.A: Stationary conditions for the helical phase
V.A: Stationary conditions for the helical phase

answers.answer: Supported. The transverse stiffness is n_s^{yy}=(4m/ℏ²)∂²Ω_hel/∂Q² and vanishes on the leading-order LT line a=0, while n_s^{xx} remains finite. Helical metastability against additional modulation is determined by the lowest fluctuation eigenvalue ε_1(q), with ST′ defined by min_q ε_1(q)=0, ∂_qε_1(q)=0, and the helical gap equations. The emerging branch is described as three-exponential and is expected to evolve toward the parity-even stripe state. Near T_c, κ=0.0053>0, supporting a second-order helical instability in the controlled GL analysis; away from T_c the authors allow a weakly first-order helical-to-stripe transition. These are local/Gaussian or GL stability results, not a demonstrated global free-energy comparison of every branch.

references.section: VI–VII: electromagnetic response and weakly helical phase

answers.answer: Contradicted. The source does not study an independently finite-asymmetry case δN=0.25 and does not define α-tilde. Its principal clean phase diagram neglects ν_+−ν_−, while the later correction is perturbative in α/v_F. Therefore the paper cannot be identified with the external clean parabolic Rashba model at α-tilde=0.25 by parameter relabeling alone.

references.section: VI–VII: electromagnetic response and weakly helical phase

answers.answer: Unresolved. The source has no T/T_c≈0.05 single-q weak/strong-helical critical endpoint and no exact h,q coordinates corresponding to the external Zhuang2026 claim. Its low-temperature discussion gives a first-order homogeneous-to-inhomogeneous regime and qualitative O′/ST′ statements, but not a global finite-DOS-asymmetry boundary at the external coordinates. It therefore does not demonstrably preempt that external endpoint in the stated δN=0.25 domain. Exact model conventions, branch content, and free energies must still be audited; if they are not identical, the finite-K stability question requires a new calculation.

answers.answer: Supported. The cheapest source-based remapping is to compare the external model with Eqs. (8), (22), (24)–(28), (32)–(33), and the finite-gap helical equations (53)–(60), then compare the transverse-curvature criterion (62) and fluctuation criterion (65)–(68). This can test leading-order model identity and normalization, but cannot settle global finite-K competition without evaluating the relevant competing branches. The closest cited formulations are the authors’ earlier JETP Letters work [8], the 2D LOFF treatment [9], Agterberg’s weak-helical formulation [10], Yip’s equilibrium-current analysis [20], Polyakov’s 2D fluctuation treatment [22], and Agterberg–Kaur’s clean DOS-asymmetry study [24].
